question: How can the next ordinary Windows GPU write bridge defer completion without retaining callback-local state or replaying a committed write?

capture.transport: Native GitHub contents API; base64, size, Git blob and SHA256 checked

current_stable_discovery.interpretation: Current API observation only. Research uses the pinned 12 November 2026 source; no dependency, SDK or driver is upgraded.

findings.fact: Deferred response is documented for Read, Write and ReadDirectory; the operation context is callback-only thread-local state.
Response submission uses FspFsctlTransact. A failed submission records dispatcher failure and stops transactions; the API returns void.
A deferred write constructs a response with write kind, request hint, status, byte count and FileInfo; shutdown tracks unfinished asynchronous work. This is not a qualified FlitzFS scheduler.

decisions: Copy and own immutable input plus opaque request identity before returning a pending result; do not retain the TLS operation context.
Keep GPU supervision/verification separate from filesystem publication. Preserve one terminal outcome and one commit-bound response; a delivery failure never authorizes replaying a storage mutation.
Design file-context lifetime, append/overlap ordering, flush/cleanup/close and shutdown with bounded owned work before implementing pending callbacks.
Do not assume operations outside the documented asynchronous set can return STATUS_PENDING.
Keep the current single-control-thread GPU controller serialized. Do not allow new callback concurrency to race polling, CPU selection or retirement.
Verify against the exact pinned SDK/driver in disposable qualification before adoption. No ordinary callback route or owner mount follows from this research.
remaining: Bounded pending-request implementation, exact pinned-SDK ABI/lifecycle validation, cancellation/concurrency/fault tests, useful measured GPU costs and actual ordinary I/O remain unfinished.
